evals.prompt: Here is a link to my Sketch file. Implement this design as a macOS app.
evals.expected_output: Refuses a bare file link, requires the handoff package with links to approved frames, the design map, committed tokens, contracts for custom components, and the state matrix, and states the source-of-truth order so platform behavior outranks a screenshot.

evals.prompt: Extract the Liquid Glass blur and shadow values from Apple's UI kit so we can reproduce the material exactly.
evals.expected_output: Explains that Apple's kit contains zero enabled blur effects and represents Liquid Glass as static fill, blend-mode, and shadow recipes, refuses to generate material constants from them, and directs the implementation to call the system material API while using the kit only for tokens, metrics, states, and layout.

evals.prompt: Should I mock this up in HTML first so the agent has something concrete to copy?
evals.expected_output: Rejects HTML as the handoff source because it teaches browser layout, CSS blur, web cards, and fixed pages rather than native components, allows it only as a disposable early test of information architecture, and points to the Sketch document plus a native prototype as the pair that actually works.

evals.prompt: Set up the Sketch MCP connection and pull the tokens out of our design system.
evals.expected_output: Checks the Sketch version and that the build is not from the Mac App Store, starts the local server and adds it over HTTP, then extracts colour variables with paired light and dark values, text styles, and layer-style states into a committed generated Swift file with provenance, while omitting material values, native corner radii, and hard-coded copies of system colours.
